traps.trap: FNAC is the investigation of choice for a breast lump

probes.stem_idea: Investigation of choice for tissue diagnosis of a palpable breast lump in a 45-year-old?
probes.note: the trap is the old PYQ key

probes.stem_idea: Before neoadjuvant therapy the team needs invasive versus in situ status plus ER, PR and HER2. Which sample serves?
probes.correct: Core biopsy of the breast mass
distractor_set: Frozen section at the time of surgery

traps.diagnoses: Learner holds the older key that FNAC is the breast test and has not tied the choice to what the pathologist must report.
traps.first_wrong_step: Treats cytology as sufficient for the breast mass without asking whether it can show invasion and receptor status.

repair.strategy: E5: teach both, 'PYQs expected FNAC; current practice is core biopsy because it gives histology and receptors'; FNAC kept for nodes and cysts

traps.retest: vignette about receptor status, and again in the triple-assessment consolidation
traps.report_hint: Avoided: current key secure. Recovered: they switched from the old key. Open: still answering with the old PYQ key; revise why core gives receptor status.

traps.trap: Supraclavicular node involvement is M1

probes.stem_idea: In current AJCC staging, ipsilateral supraclavicular node involvement is classed as?
probes.note: N3a and N2b are the neighbouring nodal stations

probes.stem_idea: Breast cancer with ipsilateral supraclavicular nodes and nothing else distant; give the N and M categories.

traps.diagnoses: Learner files any node above the clavicle as distant disease from the old classification.
traps.first_wrong_step: Reads 'beyond the axilla' as 'distant' instead of placing it on the nodal ladder.

repair.strategy: E5: PYQs expected M1; current AJCC says N3c; lay out the nodal ladder N1 to N3c with the anatomical position of each

traps.retest: staging vignette with a distant organ finding, and a later TNM which-is-not
traps.report_hint: Avoided: staging key current. Recovered: replaced the old M1 key. Open: still counts supraclavicular nodes as metastasis; review the N3 ladder.

traps.trap: Radical (Halsted) mastectomy is the standard surgery for operable carcinoma breast

probes.stem_idea: Current treatment of choice for operable carcinoma breast?
probes.correct: Breast conservation with radiotherapy, or MRM, by suitability

probes.stem_idea: What separates MRM from Halsted?
probes.correct: MRM keeps pectoralis major; Halsted removes it and pectoralis minor
distractor_set: Halsted spares both pectoral muscles and is the present standard
MRM leaves the axilla undissected; Halsted clears it
MRM removes pectoralis major; Halsted spares it

traps.diagnoses: Learner equates 'radical' with the definitive operation and has not updated to conservation or MRM.
traps.first_wrong_step: Chooses the most extensive operation as the most definitive without asking what survival data show.

repair.strategy: E5: PYQs expected Halsted; current practice is BCS plus RT or MRM; contrast the muscle preserved

traps.retest: muscle-contrast probe, then a BCS suitability case
traps.report_hint: Avoided: knows the surgery has de-escalated. Recovered: updated the old key. Open: still thinks bigger is better; review what Halsted removes and why it is rarely done.

traps.trap: Carcinoma cervix is the most common cancer in Indian women

probes.stem_idea: Most common cancer in women in India, current teaching?
An old PYQ key says cervix is the commonest female cancer in India. What do you answer in a current paper?
probes.correct: Breast; cervix was the older key
distractor_set: Cervix; keys do not change over time

traps.diagnoses: Learner recalls the older key and has not noticed that breast cancer has overtaken cervix.
traps.first_wrong_step: Recalls a remembered PYQ answer without checking whether the epidemiology has changed.

repair.strategy: E5: 'PYQs expected cervix; breast has since overtaken it'

traps.retest: old-key contrast probe and the final exam-traps segment
traps.report_hint: Avoided: current epidemiology secure. Recovered: updated. Open: still carries the old key; remember breast is now first in India and worldwide.

traps.trap: A bone scan or CT is part of the routine work-up of every breast cancer

probes.stem_idea: 38-year-old, 1.5 cm core-proven invasive ductal carcinoma, clinically node-negative, no symptoms. What next?
probes.correct: No routine metastatic imaging; plan local treatment
distractor_set: Baseline serum CA 15-3 as a staging test

probes.stem_idea: Patient A has early asymptomatic cancer; patient B has stage III disease with bone pain. Who needs staging imaging?
distractor_set: Neither; imaging is done only after surgery

traps.diagnoses: Learner links 'bone is the commonest metastatic site' to a routine test regardless of stage or symptoms.
traps.first_wrong_step: Moves from where metastases usually go to ordering the test for every patient.

repair.strategy: E8: ladder of who is imaged and why; early asymptomatic skips it, locally advanced or symptomatic gets it

traps.retest: contrast probe, and a locally advanced case in management
traps.report_hint: Avoided: sensible about over-investigation. Recovered: now ties imaging to stage and symptoms. Open: orders full staging for everyone; review the indications.

traps.trap: Trastuzumab cardiotoxicity is dose-dependent and irreversible like doxorubicin

probes.stem_idea: Which statement about trastuzumab cardiotoxicity is correct?
distractor_set: Seen only when given with a taxane

probes.stem_idea: Which agent causes cumulative-dose-dependent, largely irreversible cardiomyopathy?

traps.diagnoses: Learner merges two cardiotoxic drugs under one label and loses the qualifier that separates their behaviour.
traps.first_wrong_step: Transfers the anthracycline pattern to every cardiotoxic breast drug.

repair.strategy: E7: contrast the two drugs side by side on dose relation and reversibility

traps.retest: reversed-direction probe naming doxorubicin; again in the exam-traps segment
traps.report_hint: Avoided: separates the agents. Recovered: now holds the contrast. Open: still treats trastuzumab like an anthracycline.

traps.trap: Tamoxifen is the hormone of choice for every ER-positive patient

probes.stem_idea: 62-year-old postmenopausal woman, ER-positive early cancer. Hormonal drug of choice?
36-year-old premenopausal woman, ER-positive. Hormonal drug of choice?
probes.note: the reverse direction of the same cue-blindness

traps.diagnoses: Learner keys on ER positivity alone and ignores menopausal status.
traps.first_wrong_step: Stops reading the vignette at 'ER-positive' and never asks where the patient's oestrogen comes from.

repair.strategy: E7: highlight the qualifier; postmenopausal oestrogen is peripheral aromatisation, so aromatase inhibitors act; premenopausal ovarian oestrogen is blocked at the receptor by tamoxifen

traps.retest: the two vignettes are each other's retest, plus a male breast cancer or chemoprevention case
traps.report_hint: Avoided: reads menopausal status. Recovered: now checks status. Open: still uses tamoxifen as default.

traps.trap: Invasive lobular carcinoma behaves like ductal (single mass, unilateral)

probes.stem_idea: Histological type most often bilateral or multicentric?
Biopsy shows cells in single file with loss of E-cadherin; later spread to peritoneum and ovaries. Which type?

traps.diagnoses: Learner defaults to NST for every histology question because it is the commonest type.
traps.first_wrong_step: Equates 'most common' with 'the answer to any type question'.

repair.strategy: E1: side-by-side contrast of ILC and NST on pattern, cadherin, multicentricity and spread

traps.retest: cell-pattern vignette; again in the exam-traps segment
traps.report_hint: Avoided: separates the two types. Recovered: contrast now clear. Open: still defaults to NST.

traps.trap: Peau d'orange means T4d (inflammatory carcinoma)

probes.stem_idea: 3 cm tumour with peau d'orange over it, no redness or warmth. T category?
probes.note: T3 is the size trap, partial

probes.stem_idea: Red, warm, swollen breast with peau d'orange over a third of the breast, no discrete lump. T category?
probes.note: tests the reverse fall: sign without clinical picture versus picture

traps.diagnoses: Learner matches on the sign instead of the full clinical picture and merges two T4 categories.
traps.first_wrong_step: Ties peau d'orange to inflammatory carcinoma rather than to skin involvement in general.

repair.strategy: E1: contrast the two cases; peau d'orange alone is skin (T4b), T4d needs the red, warm, one-third presentation

traps.retest: the second probe, then a T-category which-is-not
traps.report_hint: Avoided: separates sign from syndrome. Recovered: now asks for the clinical picture. Open: peau d'orange still triggers T4d.

traps.trap: Invasion of pectoralis major alone is T4a chest-wall disease

probes.stem_idea: Which finding qualifies as T4a chest-wall extension?
distractor_set: Tumour fixed to pectoralis major alone

probes.stem_idea: 4 cm tumour fixed when the pectoralis is contracted, ribs and intercostals free. T category by size?

traps.diagnoses: Learner pads the chest-wall list with the muscle the tumour touches.
traps.first_wrong_step: Counts the pectoralis as chest wall, though the T4a list is ribs, intercostals and serratus.

repair.strategy: E2: rebuild the T4a set from its logic; chest wall excludes the pectoralis

traps.retest: vignette with fixity; later a which-is-not in the T4 set
traps.report_hint: Avoided: knows the chest-wall list. Recovered: removed pectoralis from it. Open: still counts muscle fixity as T4a.

traps.trap: Tumour larger than 5 cm is an absolute contraindication to BCS

probes.stem_idea: Which is a contraindication to breast-conserving surgery?
6 cm tumour in a woman with a moderate-sized breast shrinks to 2 cm on neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Can BCS be offered?
probes.correct: Yes, BCS with whole-breast radiotherapy is possible
distractor_set: No, size above 5 cm forbids BCS
No, shrinkage after chemotherapy makes margins unreliable
Yes, and radiotherapy can be omitted

traps.diagnoses: Learner carries the staging criterion of size into the surgical list.
traps.first_wrong_step: Treats size as a contraindication in its own right instead of size relative to the breast, and ignores downstaging.

repair.strategy: E2: rebuild the BCS contraindication list from its logic (cannot get clear margins, cannot give RT, or RT toxicity)

traps.retest: downstaged-tumour vignette; later a which-is-not on BCS contraindications
traps.report_hint: Avoided: list built from logic. Recovered: dropped size alone. Open: still carries size into the contraindication list.

traps.trap: Long thoracic nerve is the nerve most commonly injured in axillary dissection

probes.stem_idea: Nerve most commonly injured in axillary lymph node dissection?
After ALND a patient has numbness of the medial upper arm and no winging. Explanation?
probes.correct: Intercostobrachial nerve sacrificed, the commonest nerve injury
distractor_set: Long thoracic nerve injury, the commonest nerve injury

traps.diagnoses: Learner links the most dramatic complication, winging, to the most frequent one.
traps.first_wrong_step: Equates the nerve with the most memorable deficit with the nerve most often injured.

repair.strategy: E10: pair each nerve with its deficit, then separate frequency from drama

traps.retest: numbness vignette; later a winging-of-scapula pairing
traps.report_hint: Avoided: pairs nerve to deficit. Recovered: separates common from dramatic. Open: still picks long thoracic as most common.

traps.trap: Surgery first, then chemotherapy, in inflammatory or locally advanced cancer

probes.stem_idea: Correct order of treatment for inflammatory carcinoma?
Stage III locally advanced cancer with fixed matted axillary nodes. Initial treatment?

traps.diagnoses: Learner names the right three treatments but puts the operation first.
traps.first_wrong_step: Starts with the named operation and forgets that downstaging precedes surgery in unresectable or aggressive disease.

repair.strategy: E9: order the steps and ask what first and why (control micrometastases and shrink disease)

traps.retest: vignette on LABC; again in the final consolidation sequence
traps.report_hint: Avoided: right order. Recovered: sequence fixed. Open: operation still goes first; rehearse chemo, MRM, RT.

traps.trap: Carcinoma is the most common cause of bloody nipple discharge

probes.stem_idea: Most common cause of bloody nipple discharge?
35-year-old with single-duct bloody discharge and no palpable lump. Most likely cause?

traps.diagnoses: Learner reads 'most common' as 'most worrying'.
traps.first_wrong_step: Lets the red-flag status of the sign decide the frequency question.

repair.strategy: E4: show the exact qualifier, 'most common cause' versus 'cause that must be excluded', with the counter-case

traps.retest: vignette; again in the exam-traps segment
traps.report_hint: Avoided: separates frequency from alarm. Recovered: now keeps the qualifier. Open: still answers carcinoma for 'most common'.

traps.trap: Clinically node-negative patients need ALND first, with SLNB only if it fails

probes.stem_idea: 50-year-old, 2 cm invasive ductal carcinoma, clinically node-negative axilla. First axillary procedure?
distractor_set: Level I and II axillary dissection first

probes.stem_idea: Patient A is clinically node-negative; patient B has biopsy-proven node-positive axilla. Axillary plan for each?
probes.correct: A gets SLNB; B goes to ALND
distractor_set: A gets ALND; B gets SLNB

traps.diagnoses: Learner keeps the old order in which dissection comes first.
traps.first_wrong_step: Chooses the classical axillary operation before asking what staging the axilla needs.

repair.strategy: E9: order the steps; stage with SLNB when cN0, dissect when node-positive

traps.retest: contrast probe; later a sentinel-node case in management
traps.report_hint: Avoided: staging before dissection. Recovered: order fixed. Open: still dissects first.

traps.trap: BRCA1 is on 13q and BRCA2 on 17q

probes.stem_idea: Chromosomal locations of BRCA1 and BRCA2?
A breast-ovarian cancer family has a mutation on chromosome 17q. Which gene?

traps.diagnoses: Learner holds the pair of numbers but not which gene owns which.
traps.first_wrong_step: Recalls '13 and 17' as an unordered pair.

repair.strategy: E6: anchor the numbers to a hook, BRCA1 is the 1 and 17 shares a digit; BRCA2 pairs with 13 and male cancer

traps.retest: reverse-direction numbers probe
traps.report_hint: Avoided: numbers secure. Recovered: pair re-anchored. Open: swaps 13q and 17q.

traps.trap: BRCA1 is the gene linked to male breast cancer

probes.stem_idea: Gene most associated with male breast cancer?
Family A has triple-negative breast cancers in women; family B has breast cancer in a man. Likely genes?
probes.correct: A is BRCA1; B is BRCA2
distractor_set: A is BRCA2; B is BRCA1

traps.diagnoses: Learner attaches the more famous gene and its phenotype to every hereditary breast question.
traps.first_wrong_step: Chooses BRCA1 because it is the best-known gene, without asking which phenotype the stem describes.

repair.strategy: E10: pair each gene with its phenotype and contrast

traps.retest: two-family contrast
traps.report_hint: Avoided: gene-phenotype pairs secure. Recovered: pairs fixed. Open: BRCA1 still answers every genetics stem.

traps.trap: Mammography is the first imaging test for a woman under 35

probes.stem_idea: 27-year-old with a breast lump. Imaging of choice?
A 28-year-old and a 52-year-old each have a breast problem. Imaging of choice for each?
probes.correct: Ultrasound for the 28-year-old; mammography for the 52-year-old

traps.diagnoses: Learner carries the screening test of choice into every age group.
traps.first_wrong_step: Ignores age and breast density when picking the imaging.

repair.strategy: E7: highlight the age qualifier and contrast the two settings

traps.retest: age contrast
traps.report_hint: Avoided: reads age. Recovered: now checks age first. Open: mammography for everyone.

traps.trap: Tamoxifen protects the endometrium

probes.stem_idea: Which is a recognised adverse effect of tamoxifen?
distractor_set: Endometrial atrophy that protects against carcinoma

probes.stem_idea: Tamoxifen versus raloxifene and the endometrium?
probes.correct: Tamoxifen raises endometrial cancer risk; raloxifene does not
distractor_set: Raloxifene raises it; tamoxifen does not
probes.note: first two options share TR22 as one reversed-tissue-action error

traps.diagnoses: Learner treats a SERM as an oestrogen blocker on every tissue.
traps.first_wrong_step: Assumes anti-oestrogen effect in the breast carries over to the uterus.

repair.strategy: E3: predict then show; tamoxifen is antagonist in breast but partial agonist in endometrium

traps.retest: contrast probe; later a chemoprevention case
traps.report_hint: Avoided: tissue-specific effect understood. Recovered: reversed mechanism fixed. Open: still thinks tamoxifen protects the uterus.

traps.trap: Classic LCIS needs mastectomy

probes.stem_idea: Core biopsy of a mammography-detected area shows classic LCIS with no invasive component. Management?
Management of DCIS versus classic LCIS?
probes.correct: DCIS: BCS with radiotherapy or mastectomy; classic LCIS: surveillance
distractor_set: LCIS: BCS with radiotherapy; DCIS: surveillance

traps.diagnoses: Learner applies invasive-cancer treatment to a risk marker.
traps.first_wrong_step: Reads 'carcinoma in situ' as cancer to be removed rather than asking what LCIS predicts.

repair.strategy: E7: contrast the two in-situ lesions on what each represents (precursor versus risk marker)

traps.retest: contrast probe in the exam-traps segment
traps.report_hint: Avoided: LCIS understood as marker. Recovered: now separates marker from cancer. Open: still operates on classic LCIS.

Medium yield; CA 15-3 distractors are used as partial options in TR5 probes

probe_plan: Backbone traps are TR1, TR2, TR3, TR4 (the four outdated-key traps that anchor the exam-traps segment), TR12 and TR13 (staging look-alikes), TR7 (menopausal qualifier that drives drug choice), and TR16 and TR27 (order of treatment). Meet them in this order. First TR4, TR1 and TR17 (epidemiology and triple assessment: the diagnosis path), then TR5 and TR2 and TR12 and TR13 (staging builds on the diagnostic work-up and the T and N ladders), then TR27, TR3, TR14 and TR16 (surgery and sequence, which depend on stage), then TR7, TR22, TR6 and TR25 (systemic therapy and in-situ disease), then TR10, TR20, TR15, TR8 and TR9 (pathology, clinical and genetics, used as interleaved retests in the later segments). TR2, TR12, TR13 compete in one T and N staging stem and so share a probe family; TR3, TR14 and TR27 share surgical decisions; TR7 and TR22 share the tamoxifen stem. No distractor serves two traps; where a distractor is a neighbour of another trap's wrong answer it is marked partial. Every trap has two probes in different forms, and the second is placed in a later segment so that recovery can be credited.
